messages:
maria: Quick Q — when using a PRIVATE endpoint + HTTP proxy + a custom base URL in the Node SDK, what's the exact precedence for host selection and when does the client fallback to the public API? Seeing a few users unexpectedly hit public-api when their proxy hiccups.

sam: Short answer: private endpoint wins if configured, then custom base URL, then the default host. But proxy/env overrides can change runtime behavior. Example precedence we use: 
```
1) explicit client config: { privateEndpoint }
2) env: REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT
3) explicit client config: { baseUrl }
4) env: REDWOOD_CUSTOM_BASE_URL or REDWOOD_API_HOST
5) built-in default host (api.redwood.inference)
```
And fallback logic only kicks in on network/5xx-ish failures by default (not on 4xx auth/client errors).

liam: One nuance: TLS SNI/Host routing — if your proxy rewrites Host headers (or terminates TLS), the server may route to the public tenant. If you're tunneling mTLS through a proxy make sure the proxy preserves the Host or use SNI passthrough. Also streaming reconnections can surface this: proxy drop -> reconnect -> ends up at public because Host got rewritten.

jen: Adding customer war story: we had idle streaming killed by a NAT timeout. We pushed a keepalive/ping every 55s in the SDK and added a proxy option so the client can request host preservation. For Node config we landed on: 
```js
new RedwoodClient({
  privateEndpoint: process.env.REDWOOD_PRIVATE_ENDPOINT,
  proxy: { url: process.env.HTTP_PROXY, preserveHost: true },
  streaming: { keepaliveIntervalSec: 55 }
})
```
This avoided the NAT drop + kept SNI consistent. :thumbsup:

sam: Also: fallback triggers are configurable. If you want automatic switch-to-public for gateway/network faults you can set: 
```js
client.setFailoverPolicy({ on: ['network_error','gateway_timeout'], maxAttempts: 2 })
```
Important: we do NOT auto-failover on 401/403 — that's intentional to avoid leaking requests to public endpoints.

maria: Awesome — thanks everyone. I'll update the DevEx guide with the env var precedence, the streaming keepalive snippet, and a short note about preserveHost. @sam @jen can you ✍️ a tiny code example for Java + Node?
